q: If we lease out industrial sheds or warehouse space, do we report the tenants' electricity as Category 13?
title: Landlords and tenant electricity: Category 13
short: Usually yes. Under operational control, tenants run the sheds, so their electricity goes in your Scope 3 Category 13, downstream leased assets. Under financial control or equity share with an operating lease, it goes in your Scope 1 and 2. Electricity for common areas you run stays in your Scope 2.
audience: Owners of MSME estates, warehousing parks and commercial property in India

ul: Operating lease, operational control approach: tenant energy in Category 13.
Operating lease, financial control or equity share: tenant energy in your Scope 1 and 2.
Finance or capital lease, any approach: tenant energy in Category 13, because the tenant holds both control and the economic ownership.
Common areas you run (street lights, water pumps, security cabins, shared lifts): your Scope 1 and 2 under any approach.

sections.h: When power comes through your connection
p: Many estates take one HT connection and bill tenants by sub-meter. The kWh on tenants' sub-meters are their Scope 2 under operational control. Take them out of your own Scope 2 and report them in Category 13, so your Scope 2 covers only common areas and your own office. Keep the main meter, sub-meter totals and losses reconciled, and count each tenant kWh once: here in Category 13, not again as resold electricity in Category 3.

Scope 3 categories are included when relevant. For a company whose business is leasing space, tenant energy is often its largest Scope 3 source, so leaving it out needs a written reason. Include tenant diesel generators and other fuel use where you can get the figures.

sections.h: When tenants will not share data
ol: Use sub-meter readings you already hold.
Otherwise ask for discom bills, with names and account numbers hidden.
As a last resort, estimate from floor area x a kWh per square metre benchmark for that use, labelled as an estimate.

example.title: Worked example: an estate of 20 sheds
lines: Tenants' sub-metered electricity: 1,800,000 kWh a year
Common areas on your connection: 120,000 kWh
Tenant generators: 10,000 litres of diesel x 2.68 = 26,800 kg, about 26.8 t CO2, also in Category 13
example.note: Shown under the operational control approach with operating leases. Under financial control the 1,278 t and 26.8 t would move into your Scope 2 and Scope 1.

senseible: Senseible reads kWh from the electricity bills tenants share with you, and from your own bills, and applies the CEA factor of 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25. Your consolidation approach, and so the category, is a reporting choice you record.
